Searched PubMed and bioRxiv via the smarts.bio tool catalogue (`ncbi-pubmed`, `biorxiv-search`). Three searches, date-restricted 2025–present (today is 2026-11-03). Worth flagging up front: **PubMed returned bibliographic records but no abstracts** ("Abstract not available" on every hit), so for the journal papers below I can vouch for title/journal/date/PMID/DOI only — not for the findings. Where I state a result, it comes from the bioRxiv tool's summarization of preprint abstracts, and I mark it as such.

## The field has shifted from "can AlphaFold fold an antibody?" to "can co-folding models get the antibody–antigen *interface* right?"

### Benchmarks and head-to-head evaluations

| Paper | Venue | ID |
|---|---|---|
| Benchmarking AlphaFold and related deep learning approaches for modeling antibody and TCR antigen recognition (Yin, Pierce et al.) | bioRxiv, 2026-07-06 | PMID 42465237, doi 10.64898/2026.07.04.736425 |
| Evaluating deep learning based structure prediction methods on antibody-antigen complexes (Fromm, Ludaic, Elofsson) | *Bioinformatics* 42(4), 2026-04-07 | PMID 41863324, doi 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag136 |
| Benchmarking all-atom biomolecular structure prediction with FoldBench (Xu et al.) | *Nat Commun* 17:442, 2025-12-04 | PMID 41345395, doi 10.1038/s41467-025-67127-3 |
| Practical Outcomes From CASP16 for Users in Need of Biomolecular Structure Prediction (Abriata & Dal Peraro) | *Proteins* 94(1):435-446, 2026-01 | PMID 41088961, doi 10.1002/prot.70078 |
| Benchmarking TCR-pMHC structure prediction (Lu et al.) | *Brief Bioinform* 27(3), 2026-05-04 | PMID 42248582, doi 10.1093/bib/bbag289 |

Per the bioRxiv tool's abstract summaries: AlphaFold3 is consistently the top performer against Boltz-1, Boltz-2 and Chai-1, but antibody–antigen remains the hard case — FoldBench reports **>50% failure on Ab-Ag targets**, and AF3 specifically degrades on low-co-evolution targets. A "geometry-over-coevolution" analysis (doi 10.64898/2026.04.03.716280) argues monomer geometry, not co-evolutionary signal, drives complex assembly, which is offered as the mechanistic explanation for why antibodies are hard. A separate MSA study (doi 10.64898/2026.04.14.718427) reports MSA *depth* matters more than *pairing*.

### Scoring and model selection — the most active sub-area

Internal confidence (ipTM/pLDDT) is being reported as insufficient for antibodies:
- **ABAG-Rank** — learned ranking of AlphaFold Ab-Ag ensembles, reported to beat AF's internal scores (doi 10.64898/2026.03.17.712376)
- **EnsPlex** — combines multiple generators with FACET ranking; reported up to **+27.8% success on 102 Ab-Ag systems** (doi 10.64898/2026.09.26.754739)
- **Boltz-2 for therapeutic Ab-Ag screening** — confidence metrics discriminate binders only weakly, **ROC-AUC < 0.60** (doi 10.64898/2026.05.13.724924)
- **POISK** — 89k patent-derived records; folding models enrich binders (~72% pairwise accuracy) but **fail at epitope localization** (doi 10.64898/2026.10.24.761513)

### Restraints and integrative modeling (the main practical workaround)

- Sánchez-Marín, Giulini & Bonvin, "Combining AI Structure Prediction and Integrative Modeling for Nanobody-Antigen Complexes," *JCIM* 66(17):11445-11458, 2026-09-14 (PMID 42734515, doi 10.1021/acs.jcim.6c01301) — the HADDOCK group's AI+restraint approach
- McMahon et al., "HDX-MS-Guided computational modeling for rapid and accurate antibody-antigen interface mapping," *mAbs* 18(1):2722455, 2026-12 (PMID 42725674)
- **BepiPocket / DiscoPocket** — B-cell-epitope-derived pocket restraints boosting Chai-1 (doi 10.1101/2025.09.17.676770)

### Sampling and protocol engineering (CAPRI Round 55 cluster, *Proteins* 94(11), 2026-11)

- Gowthaman, Pierce et al., AlphaFold and docking across CAPRI rounds 47-55 — PMID 39831331
- Raouraoua, Lensink & Brysbaert, massive sampling with **MassiveFold** — PMID 39868877
- Savaş, Karaca et al., "Towards a Greener AlphaFold2 Protocol" — compute-efficient Ab-Ag modeling, PMID 40028659
- Linker et al., "Sequence Scanning Improves Accuracy for Antibody-Antigen and Molecular Glue Ternary Complex Cofolding," *ChemMedChem* 21(21), 2026-11-12 (PMID 42962292)

### New models and design-side work

**IntelliFold-2** claims to surpass AF3 in therapeutic settings (doi 10.64898/2026.02.09.704787). **AF2Dock** adapts co-folding for structure-based docking (doi 10.1101/2025.11.28.691195). On design: **SprintX** uses synthetic structural priors against antibody-design data scarcity (*mAbs*, PMID 42957427); Eshak & Goupil-Lamy review deep-learning/physics complementarity (*Methods Mol Biol* 2998:67-95, PMID 42129084); and developability work now fuses sequence-structure models for self-association prediction (*mAbs*, PMID 42420197).

**Caveats.** My first broad PubMed query returned 90 total hits, of which I inspected 12 — much of the "AlphaFold + antibody" literature is now applied work (nanobody biosensors, immunoassays) where AF is incidental, not methods work. I did not retrieve abstracts or full text for anything, so the quantitative claims above are the tool's summaries of preprint abstracts and should be verified at source before citation. Several bioRxiv items are unreviewed preprints.

## ANSWER

Recent AlphaFold + antibody-structure literature clusters into five areas:

1. **Benchmarks** — AF3 beats Boltz-1/2 and Chai-1 but Ab-Ag stays the failure mode: FoldBench reports >50% failure on Ab-Ag (*Nat Commun* 17:442, PMID 41345395); Fromm/Elofsson, *Bioinformatics* 42(4), PMID 41863324; Yin/Pierce, bioRxiv PMID 42465237; CASP16 user review, *Proteins* 94(1):435-446, PMID 41088961.
2. **Scoring/ranking** — internal confidence is inadequate: ABAG-Rank (10.64898/2026.03.17.712376), EnsPlex (+27.8% success, 10.64898/2026.09.26.754739), Boltz-2 screening ROC-AUC <0.60 (10.64898/2026.05.13.724924), POISK epitope-localization failure (10.64898/2026.10.24.761513).
3. **Restraint-guided integrative modeling** — Bonvin group nanobody-antigen, *JCIM* 66(17):11445, PMID 42734515; HDX-MS-guided interface mapping, *mAbs*, PMID 42725674; BepiPocket/DiscoPocket epitope restraints, 10.1101/2025.09.17.676770.
4. **Sampling/protocols (CAPRI R55, *Proteins* 94(11), Nov 2026)** — PMIDs 39831331, 39868877, 40028659; sequence scanning, *ChemMedChem*, PMID 42962292.
5. **New models/design** — IntelliFold-2 (10.64898/2026.02.09.704787), AF2Dock (10.1101/2025.11.28.691195), SprintX (*mAbs*, PMID 42957427).

Mechanistic theme: a "geometry-over-coevolution" principle (10.64898/2026.04.03.716280) and MSA depth > pairing (10.64898/2026.04.14.718427) are the current explanations for why antibodies resist co-folding.

### New models and design-side work

**IntelliFold-2** claims to surpass AF3 in therapeutic settings (doi 10.64898/2026.02.09.704787). **AF2Dock** adapts co-folding for structure-based docking (doi 10.1101/2025.11.28.691195). On design: **SprintX** uses synthetic structural priors against antibody-design data scarcity (*mAbs*, PMID 42957427); Eshak & Goupil-Lamy review deep-learning/physics complementarity (*Methods Mol Biol* 2998:67-95, PMID 42129084); and developability work now fuses sequence-structure models for self-association prediction (*mAbs*, PMID 42420197).

**Caveats.** My first broad PubMed query returned 90 total hits, of which I inspected 12 — much of the "AlphaFold + antibody" literature is now applied work (nanobody biosensors, immunoassays) where AF is incidental, not methods work. I did not retrieve abstracts or full text for anything, so the quantitative claims above are the tool's summaries of preprint abstracts and should be verified at source before citation. Several bioRxiv items are unreviewed preprints.

## ANSWER

Recent AlphaFold + antibody-structure literature clusters into five areas:

1. **Benchmarks** — AF3 beats Boltz-1/2 and Chai-1 but Ab-Ag stays the failure mode: FoldBench reports >50% failure on Ab-Ag (*Nat Commun* 17:442, PMID 41345395); Fromm/Elofsson, *Bioinformatics* 42(4), PMID 41863324; Yin/Pierce, bioRxiv PMID 42465237; CASP16 user review, *Proteins* 94(1):435-446, PMID 41088961.
2. **Scoring/ranking** — internal confidence is inadequate: ABAG-Rank (10.64898/2026.03.17.712376), EnsPlex (+27.8% success, 10.64898/2026.09.26.754739), Boltz-2 screening ROC-AUC <0.60 (10.64898/2026.05.13.724924), POISK epitope-localization failure (10.64898/2026.10.24.761513).
3. **Restraint-guided integrative modeling** — Bonvin group nanobody-antigen, *JCIM* 66(17):11445, PMID 42734515; HDX-MS-guided interface mapping, *mAbs*, PMID 42725674; BepiPocket/DiscoPocket epitope restraints, 10.1101/2025.09.17.676770.
4. **Sampling/protocols (CAPRI R55, *Proteins* 94(11), Nov 2026)** — PMIDs 39831331, 39868877, 40028659; sequence scanning, *ChemMedChem*, PMID 42962292.
5. **New models/design** — IntelliFold-2 (10.64898/2026.02.09.704787), AF2Dock (10.1101/2025.11.28.691195), SprintX (*mAbs*, PMID 42957427).

Mechanistic theme: a "geometry-over-coevolution" principle (10.64898/2026.04.03.716280) and MSA depth > pairing (10.64898/2026.04.14.718427) are the current explanations for why antibodies resist co-folding.
